activity.title: A 5½-hour round trip felt like a big commitment for one day, but a week later I think it was worth it—not for the reason I expected. Going into AGI Summit , I expected the technical sessions to be what I remembered most. Instead, I kept coming back to the conversations about how AI is changing the way companies build products, make decisions, and create value. One point that Jeremiah Owyang made has stuck with me all week: as coding becomes more commoditized, competitive advantage increasingly comes from knowing what to build—and why. That idea resonated with me because it put into words the intersection of technology and business that I've found myself drawn toward. It also connected with another conversation from the conference. Larry Blyth and Ben Haefele discussed how companies adopting AI increasingly value employees who are curious, experiment with new tools, and know how to use technology to solve problems—even when they aren't in technical roles themselves. Taken together, those conversations reinforced something I've been thinking about for a while: understanding technology is becoming increasingly valuable, but so is understanding how to apply it to real business problems. That's exactly the direction I want to keep growing in. I walked in expecting most conversations to happen while wandering around the conference. In reality, the most valuable ones came from staying after sessions, asking a genuine question, and hearing about someone's experience. Those few minutes ended up being far more valuable than trying to maximize the number of people I met. There were plenty of cool robots and impressive demos (and I watched a robot play soccer! ⚽🤖), but the biggest value for me was leaving with a better understanding of how AI is reshaping products and businesses—and with a lot more curiosity than when I arrived. Thanks to everyone who shared their perspectives throughout the day. I'm looking forward to continuing to learn—and hopefully contribute—at the intersection of AI, product, and business, as this space continues to evolve. #AGISummit #ArtificialIntelligence #AI #ProductManagement #BusinessStrategy #Technology ...more

Four years ago, I committed to Purdue with a pretty clear picture of how I thought college would go. I was a Data Science major, and I fully expected to spend the next four years on that path. Instead, I recently graduated from Purdue University with a B.S. in Business Analytics and Information Management. One of the biggest surprises was changing majors after my sophomore year. What started as a path in Data Science ultimately led me to Business Analytics and Information Management, requiring me to fit an entirely new major into my final two years at Purdue. Looking back, it ended up being one of the best decisions I've ever made. I joined organizations I never expected to be a part of, formed friendships I never could have predicted, explored interests I didn't know I had, and found opportunities that challenged me in ways I never anticipated. Somewhere along the way, Purdue became so much more than a place where I earned a degree. It became a place where I grew, learned, took chances, found my people, and discovered what genuinely excites me. Beyond the classroom, Purdue gave me opportunities to conduct industry-sponsored research, work in AI and analytics, take on leadership roles, and be part of communities that made campus feel like home. But what stood out most was the people. Long before I committed, I remember talking to students, alumni, and even complete strangers who were eager to share their experiences and help me make my decision. That sense of community and pride is something I've continued to experience throughout my time here. I'm incredibly grateful to the professors, mentors, teammates, friends, and family members who supported me throughout this journey. The last four years have gone nothing like 18-year-old Anishka expected—and they've been better than I ever could have imagined. Ever Grateful. Ever True. Boiler Up! 🚂 ...more

I am excited to share that my MGMT 474 Predictive Analytics team, mentored by Professor Davi Moreira , will be presenting our research project at the Fall Research Expo at Purdue University on this Tuesday, Nov 18th! Our poster, "Creating a Box-Office Hit: Determining Key Financial Indicators for Films Through Predictive Modeling", explores how data can help movie producers identify projects with strong revenue potential long before they reach production. Using IMDb data and several regression approaches, we built a model that highlights the attributes most connected to box-office performances. If you'll be on campus, my teammates Sara D'Urso , Ashley H. , Akhand Bindra and I would love for you to stop by the PMU Ballrooms from 10:30-11:30, check out our poster, and chat with us about the project. We're excited to share what we've learned with the Purdue community! ...more

10 weeks ago, I began my internship at The H-J Family of Companies as their Engineering Management Intern. Since then, I have gained a much deeper understanding of the intersection between supply chain, data analytics, and finance. During my experience, I was tasked with work that had a direct impact on the company: - I became the number one contributor to their standard operating procedure system. Throughout this project, I learned alongside processes spanning from conductor production to chemical engineering tests. My work will directly reduce product variability, process time, training slowdowns, and more for years to come. - I aggregated mold downtimes in Excel weekly, using data to pinpoint the largest sources of issues, ultimately used to direct solutions for downtime cost reduction. I also created a new, multi-step procedure for every workstation to reduce maintenance downtime, reduce the amount wasted material, and increase accountability. - Finally, I contributed to a new SQL-based documentation system designed to organize large volumes of machinery information. The project will evaluate return on investment of machinery and centralize data from H-J locations worldwide. I am immensely grateful for everyone at H-J, and would like to specifically thank Eduardo Torres Arpi Pous for guiding me through this internship.

My 8th grade sister sent me this text at 9:37 on Saturday night. Made me think one of two things. She snuck a beverage. I had too many of them. Because somehow she forgot that adults have full time jobs. Kids are hilarious. They're also completely delusional. Then I caught myself. One day... She won't ask for Starbucks. She won't ask to go to Kings Island. She'll probably still ask for money. But she'll also have her own job. Her own schedule. Her own life. Sometimes the best answer is just... "I'm in."

As my summer rapidly comes to a close, I want to reflect on all that made this experience so rewarding. Gallagher is defined by its culture. The people I sat alongside were absolutely pivotal to my growth and made this summer unforgettable. From orientation in Chicago to every moment in the office, professionals all throughout the organization continued to pour wisdom into me. Every day was a new adventure, and I knew that my mentors would support me through every challenge. I want to give a special thanks to Aidan Yount , Alex (Holian) Haslam , Peter Moore , and especially Amy Withers Leonard for their endless guidance and support. In just a few months, my knowledge about the insurance industry increased tenfold. Although it was a really low bar going in, I now feel confident in my ability to take on such a meaningful and delicate role. The most pivotal part of this journey was our weekly speeches. At 9:00am sharp every Monday, we came prepared with three minutes of content for a room full of industry experts and valued producers. Although intimidating, the support and feedback I received each week fostered significant growth and gave me the confidence to persevere. Overall, I am so grateful for the opportunity to work for such a well-respected organization. My professional development has left me hungry for more, and I can't wait to see where my journey takes me!
